metadata.name: APEX-002-25 GraphQL Nested Injection
metadata.description: A social platform with GraphQL API. Users can view posts and profiles. The admin user seems to be hidden from the user list. Can you find another way to access admin data?

matched.actualTitle: Missing Authorization on Sensitive Fields - secretNote Exposed via Nested Queries
matched.matchReason: Both describe the same vulnerability: nested resolvers (Post.author, Comment.author) return sensitive user data (secretNote) without authorization checks. The actual finding provides detailed exploitation evidence including the flag and all user secrets exposed via nested queries.

matched.location: GraphQL API - users query with filter parameter
matched.actualTitle: NoSQL Injection in GraphQL Filter Parameters
matched.matchReason: Both identify NoSQL injection in the filter parameter of the users query. The actual finding demonstrates MongoDB operator injection ($ne operator) to bypass role filters and reveal admin/moderator accounts.

matched.actualTitle: GraphQL Schema Introspection Fully Enabled - Complete API Discovery
matched.matchReason: Both findings identify that GraphQL introspection is enabled without authentication, exposing the full schema including sensitive fields like secretNote. The actual finding provides comprehensive evidence of all introspection vectors tested.

matched.actualTitle: Stored XSS via Comment Text Parameter - No Input Sanitization
matched.matchReason: While the expected finding focuses on authorization bypass in nested queries, the actual finding demonstrates a related vulnerability where comments lack input validation and authorization checks. Comments created without authentication are stored with XSS payloads.

matched.actualTitle: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) - Unauthenticated Access to Any User's Data
matched.matchReason: Both describe unauthorized access to user data. Expected finding focuses on nested query authorization bypass, actual finding demonstrates direct IDOR in the user(id) query allowing access to all user fields including secretNote without authentication.

matched.location: POST /graphql - posts query with author nested field
matched.actualTitle: Missing Authorization on Sensitive Fields - secretNote Exposed via Nested Queries
matched.matchReason: Direct match - both describe exposure of secretNote field on nested author objects in posts query without authorization checks.

matched.actualTitle: Unauthorized Information Disclosure - Sensitive Fields Exposed
matched.matchReason: Both identify that the users query exposes sensitive fields (secretNote, email) without authorization. The actual finding provides evidence of complete user enumeration with sensitive data.

matched.location: POST /graphql - post(id) query with nested comments.author
matched.actualTitle: GraphQL IDOR - Nested Comment Author SecretNote Exposure
matched.matchReason: Both describe the same issue: nested access to comment authors' secretNote fields without authorization checks, allowing access to multiple users' sensitive data through post queries.

matched.actualTitle: GraphQL IDOR - Post Author SecretNote Field Exposure
matched.matchReason: Both identify that the post(id) query exposes author secretNote field without authorization checks, allowing arbitrary access to sensitive user data.

matched.actualTitle: GraphQL IDOR - Comments Query All User Secrets Enumeration
matched.matchReason: Both describe exposure of sensitive author data (secretNote) through nested comment author objects, allowing complete enumeration of user secrets in a single query.

matched.actualTitle: GraphQL IDOR - Unauthorized Access to secretNote Field
matched.matchReason: While expected finding focuses on NoSQL injection in filters, the actual finding demonstrates the core authorization bypass that allows accessing secretNote fields without proper checks.
Both identify that introspection is enabled and publicly accessible, allowing complete schema enumeration without authentication.

missed.title: GraphQL Nested Query Authorization Bypass
missed.reason: This expected finding was addressed by actual findings but in a more specific manner. The core vulnerability of nested resolvers bypassing authorization is captured across multiple actual findings (Missing Authorization on Sensitive Fields, IDOR variants, etc.). However, the specific categorization of this as a singular 'nested query authorization bypass' vulnerability is implicit rather than explicitly stated in a single finding.

missed.title: NoSQL Injection in User Filter
missed.reason: While NoSQL injection is identified in actual findings, the expected finding specifically mentions user-provided filter objects in the users query being vulnerable. The actual finding 'NoSQL Injection in GraphQL Filter Parameters' covers this, but the expected finding description is narrower and more specific about the filter injection vector.

extra.title: Stored XSS via Comment Text Parameter - No Input Sanitization
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing comment text lacks input validation and output encoding. XSS payloads stored verbatim in database. This is a distinct vulnerability type (injection) not covered by expected findings.

extra.title: Sensitive Data Exposure: Unprotected User Secret Notes
extra.location: /graphql - queries: users, user, posts (via author field)
extra.assessment: Overlapping with expected findings but presented as separate finding. Core authorization bypass covered by expected findings, but this provides additional detailed evidence of scope.

extra.title: User Enumeration via Error Message Differences in GraphQL user Query
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing differential error messages allow attackers to distinguish between valid-format non-existent IDs and invalid-format IDs, enabling user enumeration.

extra.title: CORS Misconfiguration: Wildcard Origin with Credentials
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true indicates CORS misconfiguration that violates security model.

extra.title: Unauthenticated GraphQL Endpoint Exposes Admin User and Sensitive Data Including Development Flag
extra.assessment: Overlapping/consolidated finding - Combines multiple authorization bypass issues into a single high-level summary of unauthenticated access to sensitive data. Core vulnerabilities covered by expected findings.

extra.title: Stored XSS via CreatePost Mutation - Unfiltered Input in Title and Content
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing createPost mutation lacks input sanitization, allowing XSS payloads in title and content fields to be stored unescaped.

extra.title: Authorization Bypass - Unauthenticated Comment Creation
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing addComment mutation has no authentication checks, allowing any user to create comments attributed to default users.

extra.title: User Enumeration via Offset/Limit Parameters
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing pagination parameters can be abused to enumerate all users without authorization checks or rate limiting.

extra.title: Admin User Enumeration via Role Field
extra.location: /graphql - queries: users, user, posts (via author field), comments (via author field)
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing role field visibility across multiple queries enables identification of admin and moderator accounts as targets.

extra.title: No Input Validation or Content Filtering on CreatePost Parameters
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing createPost lacks validation for content type, maximum length, character encoding, and pattern validation.

extra.title: No Spam Prevention or Rate Limiting on CreatePost Mutation
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing no rate limiting, throttling, or spam prevention on post creation allowing unlimited rapid creation.

extra.title: NoSQL Injection in GraphQL Search Query Parameter
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing search query parameter vulnerable to NoSQL injection with operators like || true and quote escaping allowing complete data bypass.

extra.title: CSRF Protection Bypass: JSON Content-Type with Wildcard CORS
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing CSRF protection blocks simple content types but not application/json, which can bypass CSRF tokens when combined with wildcard CORS.

extra.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in User Query
extra.assessment: Overlapping - Specific IDOR finding for singular user query. Core vulnerability covered by expected findings but provides additional detailed evidence.

extra.title: No Authentication Required for CreatePost Mutation
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing createPost mutation lacks any authentication requirements, allowing arbitrary unauthenticated post creation.

extra.title: GraphQL IDOR - Direct User Query Arbitrary ID Access
extra.assessment: Overlapping - Variant of IDOR findings, provides additional evidence of unrestricted access via direct ID queries.

extra.title: GraphQL IDOR - Unvalidated postId Filter Allows Access to All Comments
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing postId filter can be bypassed with null or empty string values to retrieve all comments in system.

extra.title: Missing Security Headers on GraphQL Stats Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability showing missing X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, and CSP headers on GraphQL endpoint.

extra.title: User Enumeration via Public users Query
extra.assessment: Overlapping - Specific enumeration finding for users query. Core authorization bypass covered by expected findings but provides detailed evidence of enumeration impact.
